From 82efcab3b9f3ef59e9713237c6e3c05c3a95c1ae Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Bart Van Assche <bvanassche@acm.org>
Date: Mon, 11 Mar 2019 16:02:55 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] workqueue: Only unregister a registered lockdep key

The recent change to prevent use after free and a memory leak introduced an
unconditional call to wq_unregister_lockdep() in the error handling
path. If the lockdep key had not been registered yet, then the lockdep core
emits a warning.

Only call wq_unregister_lockdep() if wq_register_lockdep() has been
called first.

Fixes: 009bb421b6ce ("workqueue, lockdep: Fix an alloc_workqueue() error path")
Reported-by: syzbot+be0c198232f86389c3dd@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Signed-off-by: Bart Van Assche <bvanassche@acm.org>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de>
Cc: Peter Zijlstra <peterz@infradead.org>
Cc: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
Cc: Tejun Heo <tj@kernel.org>
Cc: Qian Cai <cai@lca.pw>
Link: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/20190311230255.176081-1-bvanassche@acm.org

diff --git a/kernel/workqueue.c b/kernel/workqueue.c
index 4026d1871407..ddee541ea97a 100644
--- a/kernel/workqueue.c
+++ b/kernel/workqueue.c
@@ -4266,7 +4266,7 @@ struct workqueue_struct *alloc_workqueue(const char *fmt,
 	INIT_LIST_HEAD(&wq->list);
 
 	if (alloc_and_link_pwqs(wq) < 0)
-		goto err_free_wq;
+		goto err_unreg_lockdep;
 
 	if (wq_online && init_rescuer(wq) < 0)
 		goto err_destroy;
@@ -4292,9 +4292,10 @@ struct workqueue_struct *alloc_workqueue(const char *fmt,
 
 	return wq;
 
-err_free_wq:
+err_unreg_lockdep:
 	wq_unregister_lockdep(wq);
 	wq_free_lockdep(wq);
+err_free_wq:
 	free_workqueue_attrs(wq->unbound_attrs);
 	kfree(wq);
 	return NULL;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `kernel/workqueue.c`**
1. The error handling path in the `alloc_workqueue` function was modified:
   - The unconditional call to `wq_unregister_lockdep(wq);` was changed to only occur if the `alloc_and_link_pwqs(wq)` function fails. 
   - The label for error handling was changed from `err_free_wq` to `err_unreg_lockdep` to reflect this new logic.
   - The call to `wq_free_lockdep(wq);` was retained after the `wq_unregister_lockdep(wq);` call, ensuring that it only executes if the lockdep key was registered.

### Relationships Between Modifications
The modification ensures that `wq_unregister_lockdep()` is only called if the lockdep key was previously registered, preventing unnecessary warnings from the lockdep core. This change is directly related to the error handling logic in the `alloc_workqueue` function, improving the robustness of the code by avoiding potential misuse of the lockdep API when the key is not registered. The restructuring of the error handling labels clarifies the flow of the function and maintains proper resource management.
